findings.title: Escaping provider failure leaves admitted cooperative parent jobs uncancelled
findings.scenario: A real FS read is admitted with owner.signal and will reject when that signal aborts. Before it settles, provider.start rejects an actual Worker/control error. Provider retirement can observe exit, but the parent read remains pending.
trace: start catch captures execution reason only
close marks closed and cutoff clears the admission timer
close calls session.cancel/retire but never aborts owner.#controller
while #jobs.size awaits the still-live cooperative read indefinitely
findings.consequence: No caller abort or uncooperative callback is required: the supplied local signal simply never receives cancellation. Numeric result/raw failure cannot settle until external release. Admission timer is already cleared.
findings.recommendation: On fatal execution/control/profile failure, abort the invocation-owned parent-work signal as well as cancelling the provider; retain raw presence/priority. Keep normal entry cutoff non-aborting for preadmitted work, and never abort root/siblings.
findings.qualification: Static code path only. A future finite raw-owner test must label synthetic receipts; actual Worker exit proof requires separate E execution.

findings.title: FS-origin shape is accepted without genuine FsError recognition
findings.scenario: An actual bound FileSystem method rejects an ordinary own-data object {name:"FsError",message:"lookalike",code:"ENOENT",errno:-1,path:"/missing"}. It is not an instance recognized by the accepted core isFsError helper.
trace: fsDescriptor checks descriptors/name/code/negative safe errno, not isFsError
request emits fsError DTO and retains original only until delivered
delivered clears pending.failure; a guest may catch this converted error and return normally
findings.consequence: Unexpected raw failure may become an acknowledgeable guest FS error. FS call provenance excludes sinks but does not establish typed error authenticity. This is not a hostile-host containment claim.
findings.recommendation: Use the declared genuine error recognition route before finite field extraction, or obtain explicit root adjudication allowing structural FS-origin errors. Preserve existing unread stack and optional-field rules; do not replace cross-realm DTO validation with generic prototype equality.
findings.qualification: Custom fault-injection scenario, not an executed adapter attack or a claim all RealFS errors fail.

findings.title: Early usage/profile failures silently skip a granted diagnostic
findings.scenario: Valid explicitly injected provider, grants.stderrWrite=true, argv ["--inspect"] (or ["-e"] with missing operand), live signal and writable stderr.
trace: invocation throws NodeUsageError before host is constructed
diagnose has no write branch when host is undefined
cleanup completes and exitCode2 returns with no stderr write
findings.consequence: The inherited bounded diagnostic profile has no line despite an explicit stderr grant. Invalid CLI still correctly avoids stdin/source/provider acquisition.
findings.recommendation: Make bounded early diagnostic output available independently of source-host construction, through the same owned sink/ledger/shared budget and raw error handling. Do not acquire stdin/VFS/provider solely to diagnose.
findings.qualification: Exact static early branch; not a measured stdout/stderr result.

questions.title: Private profile error forwarded through start loses origin
questions.scenario: services.reserve or request records a local profile failure; a provider faithfully propagates that rejected operation through start(). start catch captures it again as execution and upgrades the owner origin.
questions.need: Bind whether provider must produce profileFailure versus reject for locally selected private failure, and provide a trustworthy owner disposition if needed. NodeReason alone carries present/value, not origin. Do not classify by error class/equality; externally thrown NodeProfileError must remain raw.
questions.role: Node-local handoff ambiguity/source trace, not counted as an executed bug; do not duplicate unfinished provider implementation.

questions.title: Publisher helper only captures synchronous callback throws
questions.scenario: An asynchronous publish callback returns a rejected Promise; the helper does not inspect/await its return and reports publisherFault undefined. The nine files do not call this helper yet.
questions.need: Explicitly bind a synchronous publisher-only contract and enforce it in the provider, or enroll/await real asynchronous publication and retain raw rejection. A TS void callback is not by itself a runtime completion guarantee. Future N33 must target actual publisher ownership, not a successful helper return.
questions.role: Existing helper/interface readiness question; real publisher wiring intentionally unfinished, no dynamic/typechecker claim.

questions.title: Strict field whitelist excludes a genuine FsError cause
questions.scenario: The public FsError constructor accepts ErrorOptions.cause, but fsDescriptor refuses every own field except its whitelist/stack.
questions.need: Confirm whether the finite error-transport profile intentionally leaves genuine FsError-with-cause raw. Do not blindly allow/serialize arbitrary fields. Accepted RealFS operation() reconstructs public errors without cause; therefore this review does NOT claim its ordinary missing-file route fails.
questions.role: Unscored compatibility question, not an adapter regression assertion.
